title: Trace ICE through hostile networks
description: Change the network and fallback policy. The lab shows which candidate pair wins, what was attempted first, and when TURN becomes a reliability dependency.

scenarios.label: Same local network
scenarios.detail: Peers can reach each other's host candidates without crossing a NAT.

scenarios.label: Typical home NAT
scenarios.detail: Host addresses do not cross the internet, but a STUN-discovered mapping works.

scenarios.label: Symmetric NAT
scenarios.detail: The public mapping changes by destination, so the direct server-reflexive pair fails.

scenarios.label: UDP-blocking firewall
scenarios.detail: Direct UDP and TURN/UDP are blocked; an allowed TURN/TLS listener on TCP 443 is the final path.

scenarios.label: Direct path plus TURN outage
scenarios.detail: The direct pair fails and the configured relay cannot accept the session.
